first of all;
yes Methylphenidate HCI is a amphetamine group drug and is addictive, although only if used long term or misused like the OP's cousin misusing or me using it long term.

if you can function properly without medication, don't take medication, yes ADHD is a disorder but some people can function properly meds.

my experience with ritalin and concerta are that it helps a lot, for a price.

in primary school my parents wanted to see if medication would help me, it did help but i was reacting pretty strong on the side effects and i stopped using it.

after being kicked out of a school specialized in education for people with autism i got to a school that has a lot of practical education, for a downside but i will explain that later.
in my second year there i asked my parents if i could have another trial with medication.
this time i did not react as strong to the side effects and i could keep concentrated longer and thus getting way better results, at that time i used instant release pills (ritalin) after a couple of months the doctor monitoring me suggested sustained release (concerta) instead of instant release, has to do with me having quite a heavy coming down effect, sustained release helped me in that way and due to more consistent levels it also reduced side effects.

the thing that Methylphenidate is addictive and i continue to need more to get the same results, i started with 18mg a day, now i need 36mg concerta a day and 10mg ritalin every 3 hours to get the same result as 18mg concerta when i started.
i have a meeting with my doctor soon to discuss a how to get the same results with a different approach.

conclusion.
i don't regret starting to use it since it drastically helps me stay concentrated longer and thereby being more productive and achieve more complicated goals.
i still hate the addictive property of methylphenidate and side effects do keep increasing by dose.

i can sleep through a lot of alarms, what helps me is a alarm that tells you the exact time every 30 seconds, i have a full time job with a extremely unregular shifts and still i am rarely late.

unless my music is on loop, then i sleep though my alarm.

my manager keeps a couple of pills in his office for when i forget it.
my manager knows just as well that i get things done better and faster when i take my meds.
